newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks gain 2.02 pct, industrials soar.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks gain 2.02 pct, industrials soar.

text.p: Greek shares closed substantially higher, gaining 20.38 points or 2.02 percent, with brokers predicting strong blue chip performance, especially for the banking sector and shares of OTE telecom.
"Blue chips performed well and banks recovered after estimates for a profitable 1997 were out," said George Pervanas, a broker at Pervanas Securities.
He said that tensions between Greece and Turkey due to a Cyprus decision to deploy Russian missiles slightly suppressed an otherwise positive market sentiment late last week.
Another broker said the bourse closed up, rebounding after a correction earlier in the session with trade influenced by strong performance in blue chip industrial shares.
"Shares that influence the index, like OTE, National Bank and Alpha Credit rose strongly," said broker Dimitris Matsaganis at National Securities.
Matsaganis said that institutional investors have been investing in Greek stocks in recent days, encouraged by improved inflation, interest rate cuts and the new tax on state debt paper.
The Athens general share index closed up 2.02 percent or 20.38 points at 1029.11 from Friday's 1008.73, after opening at 1008.54.
Shares of Intrasoft rose another 140 drachmas to 1,750, on recent news it had signed a four-year deal worth 3.4 billion drachmas with the informatics directorate of the EU Commission.
Banks rose 1.39 percent, construction gained 1.72 percent while small caps lost 0.56 percent. Industrials closed 3.18 percent higher while investment shares rose by 0.27 percent.
Monday's turnover was 8.3 billion drachmas on volume of 3.3 million shares. Gainers led losers 135 to 73 with 27 issues unchanged on 235 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 814.00-832.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, rose 125 drachmas to 5,025.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.97-$12.97. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 5,370-5,722 drachmas. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
